PASSO 1: O alemão escolhe pela situação: STEP 1: German chooses the preposition by the situation, and each preposition brings a case with it. STEP 2: English "to" becomes nach, zu or in depending on the destination, and "in" can be dative or accusative depending on movement. And "I've been studying for three months" uses the present in German, never a past tense. STEP 3: a preposition never comes alone — it comes with a case. Learn the two together.

PASSO 1: cinco preposições pedem SEMPRE: STEP 1: five prepositions ALWAYS take the accusative: durch (through), für (for), gegen (against; around, about — with times), ohne (without) and um (around; at — with clock times). Learn them as a chant: durch, für, gegen, ohne, um (a classic memory hook is "DOGFU"). STEP 2: remember that in the accusative only the masculine changes (den, einen, keinen). STEP 3: common contractions: durch das = durchs, für das = fürs, um das = ums. STEP 4: «gegen» also gives approximate times: «Wir kommen gegen acht Uhr» (we'll come around eight).

As nove preposições de duas vias: a regr: The nine two-way prepositions: the golden rule
PASSO 1: nove preposições mudam de caso: STEP 1: nine prepositions change case depending on the question: an, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, zwischen. STEP 2: GOLDEN RULE: if the question is WO? (where — NO movement toward a goal), use the DATIVE; if it's WOHIN? (where to — MOVEMENT toward a goal), use the ACCUSATIVE. STEP 3: in this session, the three most common: «in» (in, into), «an» (at, on — touching a vertical surface), «auf» (on, onto — on top of a horizontal surface). STEP 4: contractions: in dem = im; an dem = am; in das = ins; an das = ans; auf das = aufs. STEP 5: the article shows the difference: masculine Wo? «dem», Wohin? «den»; feminine Wo? «der», Wohin? «die»; neuter Wo? «dem», Wohin? «das». STEP 6: careful: «Ich bin im Garten» (I'm in the garden — location) × «Ich gehe in den Garten» (I'm going into the garden — movement).
o português usa preposições diferentes (: English often marks the difference with two words: "in" vs "into", "on" vs "onto". German uses the SAME preposition («in», «auf») and lets the case show whether there's movement: «im Garten» = in the garden, «in den Garten» = into the garden.

PASSO 1: as seis restantes seguem a mesm: STEP 1: the remaining six follow the same rule: hinter (behind), neben (next to), über (above, over), unter (under, below), vor (in front of), zwischen (between). STEP 2: «Wo?» takes the dative: «Die Tasche steht vor der Tür» (the bag is in front of the door). STEP 3: «Wohin?» takes the accusative: «Ich stelle die Tasche vor die Tür» (I put the bag in front of the door). STEP 4: «zwischen» needs a plural or two items: «zwischen den Büchern» (Wo?), «zwischen die Bücher» (Wohin?).
